sources.locator: "Japanese Instrument of Surrender", revision 1371613000, § lead; and "Potsdam Declaration", revision 1371052620, § lead

explanation: The declaration is, by its own formal title, the "Proclamation Defining Terms for Japanese Surrender", and the instrument is the acceptance of those terms: the English article on the instrument describes the 15 August broadcast as "the radio broadcast announcement of the acceptance of the terms of the Potsdam Declaration", which the signing of 2 September formalised. The declaration set what a surrender would have to say; it is not by itself what made Japan surrender, and this edge claims only the first.
